title: MeetingMiner eval ground-truth manifest (one scripted meeting)
description: Contract for one YAML file under evals/ground-truth/, formalizing eval-design.md §1. The manifest declares what a scripted meeting should produce and is the recall denominator: expected screenshot count = slides (or screens) + participant_segments. Independence rule: the manifest is authored from the meeting script and never derived from pipeline output - a denominator built from what the extractor emitted cannot contain a screen it missed, so it would report 100% while measuring nothing. `meeting.archetype` selects the section: ui-demo declares `screens` and must not declare `slides`; slide-deck declares `slides` and must not declare `screens`. `meeting.source_id` is the ingested drop's sourceId (docs/source-drop.schema.json), and it is how a manifest is matched to a meeting; only meetings tagged `corpus: scripted` are ever eval subjects. This schema carries shape, enumerations and required-ness only. The rules it cannot express - anchor uniqueness after normalization, id uniqueness, `qa.expected_moment` resolving to a planted id, timestamps falling inside `duration_minutes`, and source_id uniqueness across manifests - are enforced by evals/harness/groundtruth.py and reported alongside these.

meeting.description: Identity and framing of the scripted meeting the manifest describes.

id.description: The manifest's own human-facing label (e.g. demo-001). Appears in eval reports. Unique across evals/ground-truth/ - a loader rule, not a schema rule.

source_id.description: The drop's sourceId, as it appears on GET /meetings. This is the join key between a manifest and an ingested meeting. It is not knowable until the scripted meeting is recorded and pulled, so shipped fixtures carry a placeholder value and the subject selector reports the manifest as unmatched until the real id replaces it.

archetype.description: Which section carries the expected captures. ui-demo -> `screens`; slide-deck -> `slides` (a deck shows ALL its slides, so the slide list is a full manifest).

duration_minutes.description: Scripted meeting length in minutes. Bounds every timestamp in the manifest (a loader rule) and is the over-capture guardrail's denominator in eval-design §2.2.

participants.description: Who is in the scripted meeting, by script - not by transcript attribution.

role.description: The participant's role in the script, e.g. presenter.

slides.description: slide-deck archetype only: the full slide manifest. Every slide is an expected capture.

screens.description: ui-demo archetype only: every distinct application screen the script demonstrates. Each is an expected capture. `shown_at` is required here and optional on `slides`, matching eval-design §1: a demo walks screens in an order only the script knows, and checks 2.3 (view classification) and 2.5 (citation timestamp window) both need the moment an entry was on screen. A deck is shown front to back, so a slide can be placed without one.

participant_segments.description: Expected captures beyond slides/screens: the moments where no content is shared and the gallery/participant view is what a capture should hold (meeting start, the moment sharing stops).

label.description: Why this segment is expected, e.g. 'meeting start' or 'sharing stops'. Reporting only.

planted.description: Items deliberately planted in the script so extraction and retrieval have a known answer. Ids are referenced by `qa.expected_moment` and must be unique across all three lists (a loader rule).

action_items.description: Action items spoken in the script, verbatim.

decisions.description: Decisions spoken in the script, verbatim.

phrases.description: Verbatim phrases planted for transcript, timestamp and full-text index checks (eval-design §2.10).

qa.description: Questions the corpus must answer with citations. `expected_moment` names the planted item the top citation must resolve to (eval-design §2.8).

expected_moment.description: The id of a planted action item, decision or phrase. A reference no planted item declares is a validation error (a loader rule).

answer_must_contain.description: Terms the answer must contain, checked by the judge rubric in eval-design §2.7(c).

then.description: A ui-demo declares `screens`. Declaring `slides` here is an authoring mistake: the archetype and the section have to agree, or the recall denominator counts the wrong things. The forbidden section is expressed through `propertyNames` rather than `not: {required}` so that the validation message is the offending key itself instead of a dump of the whole manifest.

A slide-deck declares `slides`. Declaring `screens` here is an authoring mistake: the archetype and the section have to agree, or the recall denominator counts the wrong things. The forbidden section is expressed through `propertyNames` rather than `not: {required}` so that the validation message is the offending key itself instead of a dump of the whole manifest.

timestamp.description: Offset from meeting start as HH:MM:SS. The shape is checked here; that the clock time is real (minutes and seconds 00-59) and lands inside `meeting.duration_minutes` is a loader rule.

ocr_anchor.description: Distinctive on-screen text a capture of this slide/screen must contain - plant it on the slide if it does not occur naturally (eval-design §1 authoring rule). Required on every slide and screen, non-empty after normalization, and unique within the manifest after normalization (lowercase, punctuation stripped, whitespace collapsed - the same normalization capture-recall matching uses, so two anchors check 2.1 could not tell apart are rejected at authoring time). Uniqueness is a loader rule; JSON Schema cannot express it. KNOWN RESIDUAL RISK: uniqueness here is exact match after folding, while check 2.1 matches fuzzily at token-set similarity >= 0.8. Two anchors that differ by one word - "Order Search Results" and "Order Search Filters" - are accepted here and may still be conflated at run time. No distinctiveness threshold is invented to close that gap, because a wrong threshold would reject valid ground truth; the check that owns the threshold (5.2) inherits the condition, and a capture-recall failure whose matched entries look interchangeable should be triaged as a ground-truth script error before it is treated as a pipeline bug.

text.description: What is said, verbatim as scripted.
